newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland sets up three special economic zones.
newsitem.headline: Poland sets up three special economic zones.

text.p: The Polish government passed on Tuesday a regulation setting up special economic zones in three areas to spur investment in regions hit by high unemployment or facing industrial restructuring, its press office said.
It said in a statement the zones, which would offer income tax reliefs to investors, would be created in southwestern Legnica and Walbrzych provinces and the central Lodz province.

It said the Legnica zone covering a 382 hectare area, would help utilise real estate left behind by Russian troops, who had been stationed there since World War Two, and reduce the region's dependency on the KGHM Polska Miedz copper concern.
The government said it expected the new zone to create 15,000 new jobs by offering 10-year tax breaks for companies investing an equivalent of at least 850,000 Ecu.

In the mining region of Walbrzych, threatened by pit-closures, the 256.4-hectare zone which will grant 10-year income tax relief to firms investing at least 500,000 Ecus, is expected to create 6,000 new jobs.

The Lodz zone is designed to reduce the dominance of the textile industry and encourage development of high-tech companies in the region. The government plan assumes that 9,700 new jobs will be created over the next 20 years in the region.
Tax relief will be offered to companies investing at least two million Ecu.

Poland has been already operating similar zones in the northeastern rural province of Suwalki and in the southern industrial and mining region of Upper Silesia with the latter attracting most investment including Adam Opel's 500 million mark auto plant.
